metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Phichit–Phetchabun road trip in Thailand: drive from riverside Phichit up to Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek for the sea of fog, temples, and Lom Sak eats — with a real timetable and budget.

h1:
Phichit–Phetchabun
From Riverside Towns to the Khao Kho Sea of Fog
intro: Phichit and Phetchabun sit right next to each other — barely two hours apart by car — but they feel like two different worlds. Phichit is a town along the Nan River, full of old temples, wide lakes, and the legend of Chalawan the crocodile. Phetchabun is mountain country: the Khao Kho sea of fog, Phu Thap Boek (the highest point in the province), and cool air for most of the year. We've laid this out as a 3-day, 2-night trip that starts slow in Phichit town, then gradually climbs into the hills, and finishes with food and souvenirs in Lom Sak.
chips: 🌫️ Khao Kho & Phu Thap Boek fog

blocks.html: The best driving trips usually aren't one long straight run — they're the ones where the landscape changes in front of you. Phichit–Phetchabun is exactly that kind of route. You leave the flat Nan River plains around Phichit, and the road slowly lifts you into the Phetchabun valleys. By the time you reach Khao Kho, you hit cool air and a sea of fog that's hard to believe sits only half a day's drive from Phichit town.

We planned this for people driving their own car (or a rental), because up on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek there's almost no public transport to connect with. If you don't have a car, rent one in Phitsanulok or Phichit before heading up. The window when the fog is really pretty and the air genuinely cold is November to February. Come in the rainy season (July to September) and you'll get flower fields and lush green views instead — just pack a rain jacket and watch for slippery roads on the climb up Phu Thap Boek.

items: Day 1 — Explore Phichit town: Bueng Si Fai lake and the Chalawan legend, Wat Tha Luang (Luang Pho Phet), Wat Pho Prathap Chang, then drive into Phetchabun town (Phichit to Phetchabun is about 130 km / 2 hr).
Day 2 — Up to Khao Kho: Phra Borommathat Chedi Kanchanaphisek, Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, the Khao Kho Memorial, fog viewpoints, and a coffee-farm café (town to Khao Kho is about 30–50 km).
Day 3 — Phu Thap Boek at dawn for sunrise, then down to Lom Sak for good food and to buy sweet tamarind and souvenirs before driving home.

blocks.title: The Driving Route
blocks.html: From Phichit, take Highway 113 through Chon Daen, then Highway 21 north into Phetchabun. The main roads are good, but the climb up Khao Kho (Highway 12, turning onto 2196) is a winding mountain road. Fill the tank before you head up and make sure your brakes are in good shape.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Phichit: lakes, old temples, then on to Phetchabun

items.activity: Start at Bueng Si Fai, a large freshwater lake in the middle of town. Walk the lakeshore, see the Chalawan station (a giant crocodile statue from the Krai Thong–Chalawan legend), and take photos early before the sun gets harsh.
items.note: Free entry; there are cafés and lakeside restaurants for breakfast.

items.activity: Head to Wat Tha Luang on the Nan River to pay respects to Luang Pho Phet, an old bronze Buddha image that is Phichit's most revered.
items.note: The temple is central and easy to park at; you won't need long here.

items.activity: Lunch in Phichit town — try a long-running noodle shop or a riverside river-fish restaurant along the Nan.
items.note: See our Phichit food article for more.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Pho Prathap Chang, an Ayutthaya-era temple and the birthplace of King Suea, with old architecture worth a slow wander.
items.note: It's just south of Phichit town.

items.activity: Set off for Phetchabun, about a 2-hour drive as the landscape starts turning into valleys.
Check in to a place in Phetchabun town, walk the evening market, and try fresh sweet tamarind and local snacks.
items.note: Staying in town the first night is easier than driving up the mountain in the dark.

blocks.title: Why stay in town the first night
blocks.html: The road up Khao Kho is winding and pitch-dark at night. Staying in Phetchabun town the first night and heading up in the morning is much safer — and you get to try the food in town too.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Khao Kho: Sea of Fog and Temples

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Climb Khao Kho — temples, views, and a café stop

items.activity: Leave town early and drive up Khao Kho. The mountain views keep opening up along the way.
items.note: The air gets noticeably cooler as you climb.

items.activity: Phra Borommathat Chedi Kanchanaphisek, a white pagoda on a hilltop and Khao Kho's main place of worship, enshrining Buddha relics. The view around the chedi is wide open.
items.note: It sits right on Highway 2196 with easy parking; open daily.

items.activity: Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, a hillside temple decorated with bright tiles and ceramics, with a five-peaked chedi and mountain views — a hugely popular photo spot.
items.note: Dress modestly; it gets crowded on weekends, so going early is easier.

items.activity: Lunch at a restaurant or mountain-view café. Khao Kho has plenty of cafés set in coffee farms to choose from.
items.note: Many of them grow their own Khao Kho arabica.

items.activity: The Khao Kho Memorial, where you can learn about the fighting on Khao Kho between 1968 and 1982 (B.E. 2511–2525), with a weapons museum and a viewpoint.
items.note: Small entry fee; the history here is genuinely interesting.

items.activity: B.N. Farm / the Khao Kho flower fields and the wind-turbine viewpoint. Walk around and take photos — in the rainy season there are purple verbena fields.
items.note: The flower fields change with the season, so check before you go to see what's blooming.

items.activity: Check in to a resort on Khao Kho, relax, and wait for the sunset views and cool evening air.
items.note: Nights are genuinely cold in winter — bring a warm jacket.

blocks.html: Khao Kho is easy to explore because the sights are close together and the main roads are good. The real draw is the morning sea of fog and the cool air. If you come in winter, get up a little early and you'll catch the fog drifting through the valleys. And if you're into temple visits, you can pay respects at several relics in a single day.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Phu Thap Boek and Lom Sak

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Sunrise on Phu Thap Boek, then down for Lom Sak eats

items.activity: Get up before dawn and drive up Phu Thap Boek, the highest point in Phetchabun (1,768 m), for the sunrise and the sea of fog over the Hmong cabbage terraces.
items.note: The final stretch up Phu Thap Boek is very steep — drive carefully. If you're not confident in your car, there are local trucks that take you up.

items.activity: Have a mountain-view breakfast on Phu Thap Boek, then walk around and photograph the terraced cabbage fields.
items.note: It gets crowded in winter and lodging books up fast, so weekdays are easier.

items.activity: Head down the mountain toward Lom Sak district.
items.note: Use low gear on the descent to help the brakes.

items.activity: Lunch in Lom Sak — try the famous wonton noodles or fresh-noodle khanom chin in the Tai Lom style, with a distinct local flavor.
items.note: Lom Sak and Lom Kao are the food districts that Phetchabun locals swear by.

items.activity: Buy souvenirs to bring home: Lom Kao sweet tamarind, Rai Kamnan Jul fermented fish (pla som), and Khao Kho macadamia.
items.note: Lom Kao has a big sweet-tamarind market with better prices than buying in town.

items.activity: Set off home — and that wraps up the Phichit–Phetchabun trip.

blocks.title: You can trim it to 2 days, 1 night
blocks.html: If you're short on time, cut the Phichit town day and drive straight up to Khao Kho on day one. Stay one night on the mountain, do Phu Thap Boek the next morning, then head down to Lom Sak — you'll still hit all the mountain highlights.

blocks.text: Where to Stay, Night by Night

items.name: First night — Phetchabun town
items.blurb: Staying in town is convenient, close to the evening market and restaurants. It's a good base after a full day exploring Phichit, before heading up the mountain in the morning.

items.name: Second night — a resort on Khao Kho
items.blurb: Stay among the pine forest and coffee farms and wake up to mountain views and cool air. Pick somewhere near a viewpoint to make the morning easier.

blocks.html: In winter (December–January), lodging on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek books up fast and prices climb, so reserve several weeks ahead. Accommodation in Phichit and Phetchabun towns is easier to find and cheaper, which makes it a good base for the first night.

items: Lodging, 2 nights — 1 night in town + 1 night on Khao Kho, roughly ฿1,800–4,500 total (depending on season and resort level).
Food — about ฿80–250 per meal per person, roughly ฿1,500–2,500 over the three days.
Attraction entry — mostly free or a few baht; a few charge, such as the Khao Kho Memorial.
Souvenirs — sweet tamarind, macadamia, pla som — however much you buy.

blocks.title: What to pack for winter
blocks.html: On Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek in winter, morning temperatures can drop into single digits. Bring a warm jacket, a hat, and gloves, and fill the tank before you head up — there are few gas stations on the mountain.

faq.q: Is the drive from Phichit to Phetchabun long?
faq.a: From Phichit town to Phetchabun town it's about a 2-hour drive, roughly 130 km, via Highway 113 then 21. The main roads are good. The climb up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek is winding and adds extra time.

faq.q: How many days should a Phichit–Phetchabun trip be?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just right — one day in Phichit town, then two days up on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek. If you're short on time, make it 2 days and 1 night by cutting the Phichit town day and heading straight up to Khao Kho.

faq.q: When is Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek at its best?
faq.a: November through February is winter, when the air is cool and you have the best chance of catching the morning sea of fog. In the rainy season (July–September) the views are lush green with flower fields, but the roads are slippery, so drive carefully.

faq.q: Do I need my own car?
faq.a: We recommend having your own car or a rental, because up on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek there's almost no public transport to connect with. If you don't want to drive, you could hire a car with a driver, or use the local trucks for the steep climb up Phu Thap Boek.

faq.q: What's the best souvenir from this trip?
faq.a: Lom Kao sweet tamarind is number one, followed by Khao Kho macadamia, Rai Kamnan Jul fermented fish (pla som), and Tai Lom woven textiles. You can buy them at the Lom Kao market or souvenir shops in Phetchabun town.
